clue.text: Starting for club and a fight? About time! I'll get you a taxi

indicators.note: the starting letter is what the word club contributes here
the fight word goes round the time abbreviation, so About signals a container

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in a boxing bout

explanation.surface: Someone touts a club, picks a fight, then impatiently promises a cab home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts BOUT round T to make BTOUT. A cab-tout touts for taxi custom, so the closing words define him.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab-tout is a person who solicits passengers and finds them taxis, so he offers to get you one.

clue.text: Copper couple with jolly caterpillar

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a couple is two
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A policeman and his partner go out with a cheerful caterpillar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element; 'jolly' is a naval nickname for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a moth larva, a caterpillar that cuts through plant stems at ground level.

clue.text: Doing better than before in destruction of 78s?

definitions.meaning: setting new bests in a sport or field
literally smashing old gramophone discs that played at 78 rpm

explanation.definitionFit: Setting new bests means surpassing previous marks, and also literally smashing gramophone discs.

clue.text: You get nothing for nothing in French pictures to align

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing
rien is French for nothing
the Tate is the London gallery of pictures

explanation.surface: A sardonic remark that art in France gives you nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You get' and 'for' are link words; the TATE is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient something is to align or position it relative to a reference point or direction.

clue.text: Arch-emperor?

definitions.meaning: a triumphal arch in the Roman Forum bears this name
a Roman ruler of the first century AD

explanation.definitionFit: The Arch of Titus in Rome commemorates the emperor Titus, who reigned from 79 to 81 AD.

clue.text: Bird of the quickest relative speed

indicators.note: the bird is formed of letters inside the following phrase, so of signals a concealed run

explanation.surface: A claim about which bird flies fastest relative to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points into quicKEST RELative, where the bird sits across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon, a familiar hovering bird of prey.

clue.text: Unofficial thumping for most of party in Ireland (Northern)

parts.note: KO is a knockout, the result of a thumping

indicators.note: the larger part of the party name is kept, its second word dropped

parts.note: Fianna Fail is a major political party in Ireland

explanation.surface: A rogue attack on most of an Irish party in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unofficial' is read as UN official, a United Nations office-holder; the theme is Secretaries-General. 'most of' trims FIANNA FAIL to FIANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Kofi Annan served as Secretary-General of the United Nations, its chief official, from 1997 to 2006.

clue.text: Where some African countries are off the leash

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Countries have slipped their lead, as if they were dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LEASH; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The semi-arid belt south of the Sahara spans nations such as Mali, Niger and Chad.

clue.text: Teased Tory leader to provoke left-wing philanthropist

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or provoke
red is a byword for left-wing politics

explanation.surface: A Tory leader is mocked into angering a socialist benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ragged-Trousered Philanthropists is Robert Tressell's socialist novel, so the answer describes the philanthropist of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective qualifies the noun in the title of Tressell's novel about exploited house-painters.

clue.text: Free range item cooked by litre

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored, rearranged

explanation.surface: A free-range product prepared by the litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BY LITRE; 'item' is a link. The free-range surface tempts toward eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom to roam where one likes is the sense of free range, which is personal freedom.

clue.text: Oratory fought fight, beat beast, missing bus at random

indicators.note: the letters of bus at are to be taken away from the pool of the four words
at random means the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A garbled account of a brawl and a beaten animal, with someone missing their bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool the letters of FOUGHT FIGHT BEAT BEAST (20), remove B, U, S, A, T ('missing bus at'), and rearrange the remaining fifteen ('random'). The 'at' of 'at random' is fodder, not indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a fluent, persuasive way of speaking is the idiom's meaning, which is skill in oratory.

clue.text: Head of operations with a knowledge of wood

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from operations

parts.note: ken means range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: A head of operations who knows all about timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means made of oak, a kind of timber, so it describes something wooden.

clue.text: Half a pint?

parts.note: read literally as a modest measure of ale, but the phrase names something trivial or unimportant

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a trivial matter; literally, weak or small ale, which a half-pint glass suggests.

clue.text: Mexican actor on day one away from insurgent body

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

indicators.note: one is taken out of the insurgent group, so away from signals a removal

parts.note: the Taliban are an Afghan insurgent movement
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An actor from Mexico appears one day, distanced from a rebel group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes I from TALIBAN to leave TALBAN; 'on' joins MON to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricardo Montalban was a Mexican-born film and television actor, known for Fantasy Island.

clue.text: Unofficial financiers, one body

parts.note: a bank is a body of financiers
I is the Roman numeral for one
the moon is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: Unlicensed moneylenders forming a single organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unofficial' is read as UN official, a United Nations office-holder; 'body' is a celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: Ban Ki-moon was Secretary-General of the United Nations from 2007 to 2016.

clue.text: Poor quality drinking water in river

indicators.note: the drinking-water abbreviation sits inside the river name

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
TT means teetotal, someone who drinks only water

explanation.surface: Drinking water from a river is of doubtful quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking water' describes a teetotaller, abbreviated TT; the Tay is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby, worn and cheap-looking, describing goods of low standard.

clue.text: Unofficial effort to prove missing one false?

parts.note: a try is an effort or attempt

indicators.note: one is dropped from the verb, so missing signals a removal

parts.note: give, completed by lie, makes the idiom give the lie to, meaning prove untrue
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lie is something false

explanation.surface: An informal attempt to show that one's missing story is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unofficial' is read as UN official. To give the lie to something is to prove it false; 'missing' takes I out of GIVE, leaving GVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trygve Lie of Norway was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations, 1946 to 1952.

clue.text: Smith's fake

definitions.meaning: a smith's workplace, the smithy with its furnace
to counterfeit, as a ... copies a signature

explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith works at a forge, and to forge a document is to counterfeit it.

clue.text: Cooler part of house, say, for extreme enthusiast

parts.note: a fan cools the air

indicators.note: say signals that the room is given by how it sounds, not spelt

parts.note: an attic is the room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: Swap the fan for the loft space and you have a zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives ATTIC by sound, written ATIC; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot whose devotion is excessive is an extreme enthusiast.

clue.text: Grandma's shot at milk producer

parts.note: nanny is a child's word for grandmother, with the 's read as is
a go at something is an attempt or shot at it

explanation.surface: An old lady takes a pot-shot at a dairy animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat is kept for her milk, so she is a dairy producer.

clue.text: Couple looked unlike Cyclops

parts.note: a couple is two
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A pair gazed at something, unlike a one-eyed giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclops in Greek myth had a single eye, so having a pair is the opposite of him.

clue.text: React badly in a number of fruit

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes inside the number

parts.note: nine is a number

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of react are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone reacts poorly to several pieces of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number of fruit' tempts as a quantity, but the number is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach, eaten as a fruit.

clue.text: A bit of 8 first line of defence

parts.note: the first three letters of the answer to 8 down
I is one, the numeral for first

explanation.surface: Part of a freedom clause serves as the first barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 8 is LIBERTY, so a bit of it is LIB; 'first' is I as number one.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, an accused person's line of defence.

clue.text: Life in Rome after English musical

indicators.note: the Latin word comes after the abbreviation

parts.note: vita is Latin for life

explanation.surface: An English musical about life in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places VITA following E; Rome signals the Latin language.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Peron is a well-known musical.

clue.text: Explorer's name and number for unfinished course

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: the last letter of the racecourse is dropped

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: A traveller's name and number given out for a course left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the T of ASCOT, a Berkshire racecourse, leaving ASCO. 'and' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama, the Portuguese navigator who reached India by sea, had this first name.

clue.text: Sea, it's said, as religious article

annotationWithheld.why: Sea, it's said, as religious article (7): C (sounds like 'Sea') + AS + PI + AN, but 'Sea' must then also be the definition, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Sea, it's said, as religious article

clue.text: Changed agreement performed as reported

parts.note: amen is said to express agreement or assent

indicators.note: the word for performed is given by its spoken sound

parts.note: did means performed, as in did a dance

explanation.surface: An agreement was carried out, as the news has it, and altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as reported' turns DID into the sound written DED, as in a clipped pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to alter it, so amended means altered.
